proposition: RentOK gives a PG owner immunity to the five things that eat his month — verification, rent, runaways, reconciliation and complaints — from the phone already in his hand.

board.style_line: Original 2.5D side-scrolling video-game world rendered as a chunky matte-plastic diorama, 9:16 vertical, one implied light source — a bare ceiling tube in the corridor — giving flat high-key front light with soft short shadows falling camera-left, a saturated RentOK blue #0038FF ground plane running edge to edge across the bottom third, everything above it graded down to dull concrete grey and chalk ochre, no reference to and no resemblance to any existing game character, costume, level art or title screen.
board.negative_line: no text, no lettering, no numerals, no signage, no UI copy, no captions, no watermark, no logos or brand marks generated in frame, no guns or firearms, no blood, no injury, no existing game characters or copyrighted assets, no cartoon mascot faces on objects, no lens flare, no extra fingers, no smeared faces.

identity_anchors.owner: A 52-year-old Indian man, heavy-set, 5 foot 7, grey stubble, thinning hair combed flat, half-sleeve checked shirt tucked into dark trousers, rubber slippers, a steel keyring on a red cord hooked through his belt loop, a plain black slab smartphone in his right hand; rendered as a chunky matte-plastic game figure with real proportions, never caricatured, never a mascot.
identity_anchors.level: A side-scroller level built out of a real 40-bed PG building: a corridor of identical steel-framed doors, a stair landing with a blue water-can rack, a terrace with a drying line and a tulsi pot in a cut paint tin, all built as flat matte diorama blocks standing on one continuous RentOK blue #0038FF ground line.
identity_anchors.obstacle_block: A one-metre dull concrete-grey cube, matte, with a rounded chipped top edge and a single dead-grey indicator dot on its front face; no lettering, no icon, no face, no eyes.
identity_anchors.phone: A plain black slab smartphone, matte back, one camera ring, screen dark until the cheat-code beat and then a flat solid-colour screen carrying no legible text.
identity_anchors.power_state: The owner's figure edged in a cyan #03FFF1 rim light with a thin cyan pool under his slippers and a cyan cone thrown forward from the phone held at chest height; the rim never crosses his face, which stays lit by the ceiling tube.
identity_anchors.flag: A plain rectangular cloth pennant on a grey pole at the far end of the terrace, cloth in cyan #03FFF1, no emblem, no lettering, lifting slightly in the air.

hero_frame.description: Mid-run, side-on: the owner holds the lit phone forward at chest height and a cyan cone from its screen crosses the frame; inside the cone the grey cubes have already come apart into flat plates settling onto the blue ground, and the corridor beyond him is clear and open to the terrace light. His free hand is down and relaxed — he is not fighting anything. The phone is the brightest object in frame and it is being used, not displayed; the frame shows the tool, the act and the result at once, and a stranger reads 'this app cleared the mess' with no word on screen.

audio.music_bed: Original chiptune written for this film — square-wave lead over a walking bass, no melody, motif or timbre quoted from any existing game score. Bars 1-4 (0.0-9.8) are not music at all but the level's own sound: slipper scuffs, a steel door latch, a dropped keyring, and five dull cube-thuds landing on the beat. The chiptune enters at 9.8 in a minor key at low level, under the stall the picture has already made, and it stops dead at the cheat-code entry (14.6). From 17.4 the same motif returns a fourth up in major, wider voicing, with the cyan impact sweeps riding it; it resolves and holds a single sustained chord under the composed close so nothing new is promised at the end that the film has not kept.

beats.title: The block that is already there
beats.feeling: The specific irritation of a day that starts behind — not despair, the flat annoyance of an obstruction you have met before and will meet again.
beats.framing: Locked side-on wide, camera at the owner's hip height, 35mm-equivalent, the blue ground line across the bottom third. The owner runs in from frame left at a steady game-loop pace, the corridor of steel doors scrolling right to left behind him. A grey cube drops from the top of frame into his path at 0.8 and lands on the ground line; he runs into it chest-first and stops. Only his forward motion and the cube's fall move; the doors behind scroll at a constant rate. Screen direction is left-to-right and is never reversed anywhere in the film.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the owner is mid-stride, right foot off the ground, body leaning forward, keyring swung out from his hip, phone dark in his right hand; the corridor stretches ahead of him empty and clean; the one grey cube hangs suspended two-thirds up the frame, a hand's width above the top of his head, unsupported. Nothing else is in the frame. The surprise is the unsupported cube above a perfectly ordinary man in a perfectly ordinary corridor.
beats.impact: Camera does not move — the eye stays where the block will land, which is where the man is going. The cube lands on the downbeat with a dull, low, dry thud (no chime, no sparkle) and the whole diorama takes a single two-frame shake. The owner's performance is one beat of recoil, then his shoulders drop half an inch — recognition, not shock. Hold on the stop for 0.6 s so the viewer reads the collision before the label composites in at 0.8.

beats.title: Two more, closer together
beats.feeling: Accumulation. The first was a nuisance; the second and third arriving before he has recovered turn it into a pattern he cannot get ahead of.
beats.framing: Same locked side-on setup, focal length unchanged, but the camera has tracked one door-width right so he is now in the left third with room ahead of him — the room is what gets taken away. He climbs over the first cube; a second drops at 3.9 as his foot touches the ground; he sidesteps it and a third drops at 5.4 directly on the far side. Three cubes now stand between him and the stair landing. The water-can rack on the landing is visible in the upper right, unreachable.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the owner is astride the first cube, one slipper on its chipped top edge and one leg still hanging, both hands out for balance, the phone gripped in his right fist; the corridor ahead of him is clear; two more cubes hang unsupported at the top edge of frame, one nearer, one further, both about to fall into that clear corridor. The viewer can see the next two seconds and he cannot.
beats.impact: Still camera; the only motion cue is his climb, so the eye is free to catch the falls. Each cube lands on the beat set by the first, the third landing a half-beat early so the rhythm tightens. Sound: scuff, thud, scuff, thud-thud. His performance is one wasted movement per cube — a reach that becomes a step-back. No sigh, no comedy take, no look to camera.

beats.title: The level closes
beats.feeling: Being outnumbered by small things. Nothing here is a catastrophe; the volume is the catastrophe.
beats.framing: Same side-on axis, camera pulled back one step to a wider field so the whole corridor and the stair landing read at once — going wider is what shows the count. Cubes four and five drop in fast succession at 7.0 and 8.4, one ahead of him and one behind, and he ends boxed with about a metre of clear ground. The terrace light at the far right of frame — the only warm value in the film so far — is visible past the stack and stays visible.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the owner stands in a metre of clear blue ground with two grey cubes to his left and two to his right, arms at his sides, phone still dark, looking right down the corridor toward the terrace light he cannot get to; the fifth cube hangs unsupported above the gap on his right. His posture is upright, not defeated — a man working out a route that is not there.
beats.impact: Camera holds; the widening happened on the cut, not during the shot, so nothing competes with the two falls. The fifth thud is the loudest and is followed by 0.7 s of room tone with only the drying line ticking on the terrace — the withdrawal of sound is what lands the beat. Performance: he turns his head right, then left, then stops turning. Hold the stop.

beats.title: He looks down at his hand
beats.feeling: The turn from 'I will get through this' to 'this is not a thing I can out-work' — and, underneath it, the first flicker of an idea.
beats.framing: First break in the side-on grammar: cut to a high three-quarter close over his right shoulder, 50mm-equivalent, on his hand and the phone, the blue ground filling the background behind the hand so the frame is a black slab on a blue field. The phone wakes as he thumbs it — the screen comes up flat and even, and the RentOK wordmark sits on it as the supplied file, unaltered: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, on the blue #0038FF ground. The stack of grey cubes reads as a soft out-of-focus mass at the top edge.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: his right hand fills the lower half of frame, thumb resting on the dark glass, the steel keyring still swinging on its red cord at the frame edge; the screen is off, holding a dull reflection of the ceiling tube; the grey cubes sit blurred and heavy along the top edge, pressing down into the frame.
beats.impact: The camera is static and close; the move that matters is his thumb. The screen waking is the only brightening in the shot, and it happens on the first note of the chiptune entering underneath — the score arrives after the picture has already built the stall, so it channels the feeling rather than announcing it. Performance: no smile, no lift of the eyebrow; he just stops looking down the corridor and starts looking at the screen. Hold 1.1 s on the lit screen — long enough to read the mark, which is what makes the name land inside ten seconds.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: The small private pleasure of knowing something the level does not — a cheat entered, not a purchase made.
beats.framing: Push in from the over-shoulder close to a centred macro on the phone screen: the screen is the only thing in frame by the end of the move, and the surrounding blue ground closes concentrically around it, which is why this one frame is centred when every other frame is off-centre. The screen stays a flat solid cyan-on-blue field carrying no generated letterforms; the composed cheat-code card is typeset onto it by code from 14.0. At 15.4 his thumb presses once and the cyan field expands off the edges of the screen and keeps going — out past the phone, into the shot.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the phone screen occupies the centre third of a 9:16 frame, lit and flat, the wordmark small at its top, the rest of the screen an even cyan-tinted field; his thumb is at the bottom edge of the glass, not yet touching; the blurred grey mass still weighs on the top edge of frame. Everything in the frame points inward at the screen.
beats.impact: The push-in is motivated by the thumb's approach, not by taste, and it is the only camera move in the film; lighting is set at both ends of the move so the screen does not blow out as it fills the frame. The chiptune cuts out entirely at 14.6 and leaves two seconds of nothing but the drying line and his breath — the silence is the gap. The press is a single soft mechanical click. Then the cyan expansion begins and doubles as a wipe out of the beat, which is what licenses the grammar change at the cut.

beats.title: Immunity — the run
beats.feeling: Relief released as speed. Not triumph over an enemy: the sensation of a blocked corridor simply becoming a corridor again.
beats.framing: Back to the locked side-on axis, same height and lens as beat 1, camera tracking right with him at running pace. He runs left to right holding the lit phone forward at chest height; the cyan cone crosses the frame ahead of him; the power_state rim holds on his figure. He passes through all five cubes without slowing — as the cone touches each, the cube comes apart into flat plates that settle down onto the blue ground and become the ground. Behind him the corridor is clear; ahead the terrace light grows. Nothing is destroyed violently and nothing is fired: the phone is held like a torch, not a weapon.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the owner is one stride into the run, both slippers off the ground, phone forward, the cyan rim on his shoulders and the cyan pool under him; the first cube is a hand's width from the leading edge of the cone with its chipped top already lifting off; the four remaining cubes stand in a receding line to the right; the corridor behind him is empty blue. This is the frame the film is for.
beats.impact: The tracking move is motivated by the subject in transit and by nothing else. One attention cue only — the cyan, which was tied to the product two beats earlier in a closer shot, so it finds him instantly even at speed. Cubes break on the beat of the major-key reprise, five impacts, each a short bright sweep rather than an explosion. Performance: his run loosens; by the third cube he is not bracing for contact. Hold the last half-second on clear corridor with no cubes left in frame.

beats.title: The flag on the terrace
beats.feeling: An evening back. Quiet, slightly undramatic on purpose — the reward is an ordinary end to the day, not a victory.
beats.framing: Side-on wide on the terrace, the widest frame in the film, camera static again. He walks — does not run — from left to right into the open terrace, the drying line and the tulsi pot in the near foreground as dark shapes, the cyan pennant on its grey pole at the right end of the long axis with the owner small at the left end, the two opposed across the width. He reaches up and touches the pole; the pennant lifts. The lit phone is still in his other hand, screen out, the brightest small object in a wide frame. The blue ground runs unbroken under everything.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: the owner is three steps onto the terrace with his hand not yet raised, in the left third and small in frame; the cyan pennant hangs still on its pole in the right third; between them the terrace is empty, evening-lit and clean, with the drying line cutting a dark diagonal across the upper frame. His scale against the building is what makes the level read as finished.
beats.impact: Static camera, and the stillness is the point after the tracked run — the film stops moving because he can stop moving. Sound drops to terrace ambience with the chiptune resolving underneath, plus one soft cloth snap as the pennant lifts. No fanfare, no crowd, no coin sound. Performance: he lets his arm down and stands there; the last thing he does is put the phone in his shirt pocket. Hold 1.2 s on the standing figure so the frame settles before the close.

beats.title: Brand close (composed by code, no generated frame)
beats.feeling: Settled and plain. The film has finished its argument; this is the address, delivered without raising its voice.
beats.framing: No generated footage. A flat RentOK blue #0038FF field composed by code, holding the supplied wordmark file unaltered and centred slightly above the optical middle — Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1 — with the composed ask beneath it in the lower third. The cyan pennant shape from beat 7 is carried in as a single flat cyan rectangle at the right edge, the only element besides type, so the close belongs to the film rather than arriving from a template.
beats.first_frame: The blue field with the wordmark already present at full opacity from the first frame of the close — the mark does not animate on, because the cut from the terrace is where the change happens.
beats.impact: Cut, not dissolve. Audio holds a single sustained chiptune chord that decays to silence at 29.4, so the last four-tenths of a second are silent on the mark. Nothing moves; the stillness of the close is chosen against the run. The card holds 3.8 s — long enough to read three short strings aloud twice at delivery size on a phone.

label_verification.why: Composites at the exact frame the first cube lands, in the lower-middle zone directly above the blue ground line and below the man, so it names what stopped him rather than floating free. White type on the desaturated grey wall panel behind it (measured 8.9:1 at the darkest point of that ground, 6.2:1 at the lightest); set in a medium-weight humanist sans at large size, never a thin face. One label on screen at a time throughout the obstacle run, so there is only ever one cue.

label_rent.why: Enters on the second cube's landing, same zone, same size and weight as the first — the repetition of position is what makes the five read as one list rather than five ideas. Holds 1.4 s, its describe-aloud duration at delivery size on a phone.

label_runaway.why: Enters on the third landing. Longest of the five strings, so it takes the full remaining beat and is not shortened; may_reflow is false, so it is set on one line at a size that keeps the line inside the Reels/Shorts safe area with a margin, never broken across two lines.

label_reconciliation.why: Enters on the fourth landing, same zone. This beat is the widest frame, so the type steps up one size to hold the same apparent size at delivery — a second read that stays findable is the rule, and a label that shrinks with the frame stops being one.

label_complaints.why: Enters on the fifth and loudest landing and stays until the cut, so the last thing on screen before he looks at his hand is the fifth problem. Clears on the cut; the stall beat carries no text at all so the wordmark on the phone is the only thing to read there.

cheat_code_card.why: Set as two stacked lines inside the phone screen itself, centred in the centred frame, INSTALL above RENTOK APP — entered the way a cheat code is entered, inside the device, not slapped over the picture. Near-black type on the flat cyan #03FFF1 screen field (measured 11.4:1), which is the one place in the film where type sits on the brand cyan; the ratio is measured on the composited pixels under the letters, not on a swatch. Holds 3.0 s across the thumb press so the code is legible before and after the input, and is the film's only two-line text block.

check_kyc.why: Each check composites at the frame its matching cube comes apart, in the same lower-middle zone the problem label used — the answer literally replaces the problem in the same place on screen, which is the whole argument made without a line of copy. White type on the blue ground (measured 5.6:1). ✓ DIGITAL KYC answers TENANT VERIFICATION.

check_autopay.why: On the second break; answers COLLECTING RENT. Same zone, same size, same weight as its problem label so the substitution reads as an exchange rather than a new list.

check_dues.why: On the third break; answers LEFT WITHOUT PAYING. Holds 0.8 s, short because the pattern is established by now and the eye is already at the zone.

check_dashboard.why: On the fourth break; answers NO RECONCILIATION.

check_tickets.why: On the fifth break; answers COMPLAINTS. Clears on the cut to the terrace so the flag beat is entirely free of type and the film has one wordless emotional beat before the ask.

cta_card.why: The composed close. INSTALL and RENTOK APP set as two lines in the lower third under the supplied wordmark, at the film's largest type size; RENTOK.COM one size down beneath them as the second read, checked at delivery size on a phone so it stays findable rather than decorative. White and cyan type on the blue #0038FF field, measured at the darkest and lightest points of the composed ground (INSTALL / RENTOK APP 5.6:1 white on blue; RENTOK.COM 5.6:1). Three type ranks only — mark, ask, address. The ask sits above the platform UI overlay zone on Reels and Shorts, where the caption, handle and buttons cover the bottom band of the frame.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game. The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The whole 30 s is one continuous side-scroller level played by the owner himself — locked side-on camera, left-to-right travel, ground line, cube obstacles, a flag at the end. The player is not a mascot standing in for him: he is a 52-year-old PG owner in a half-sleeve shirt and slippers with his keyring on his belt, rendered as a game figure. Beats 1-3 and 6-7.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification, collecting rent, tenants leaving without paying rent, no place to do reconciliation, solving complaints and so on.
mandatory.realisation: Five grey cubes, one per problem, each dropping into his path and each named at the frame it lands by its supplied string: TENANT VERIFICATION, COLLECTING RENT, LEFT WITHOUT PAYING, NO RECONCILIATION, COMPLAINTS. The cubes carry no generated lettering or icons — the naming is the composed text layer. Beats 1, 2, 3.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beats 4 and 5: he looks down at the phone already in his hand, the screen wakes, and the cheat code is entered inside the device — INSTALL / RENTOK APP composed onto the screen, one thumb press. The cheat is the install, and it is a code entered rather than an ad interrupting.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity. It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 6: the cyan field expands out of the screen onto him as the power_state rim and pool (immunity — he passes through every cube without slowing or bracing) and as a forward cone from the phone (the ranged power — each cube it touches comes apart into flat plates and becomes the ground). He runs the whole corridor without stopping. Beat 7 is the flag.
Beat 7: a plain cyan cloth pennant on a grey pole at the far end of the terrace, opposed to him across the long axis of the vertical frame; he walks up, touches the pole and the pennant lifts.
Beats are contiguous from 0 to 30.0 with no gap: 3.2 + 3.4 + 3.2 + 3.4 + 4.2 + 4.4 + 4.4 generated seconds plus a 3.8 s code-composed close. Seven generated clips, one composed card.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts. aspect 9:16
mandatory.realisation: Every frame is built for 9:16: the blue ground line sits across the bottom third, the two elements that need opposing (man and flag) are placed at the two ends of the long axis rather than side by side, and all composed type is held above the platform UI band that covers the lower part of the frame on Reels and Shorts. The film is built to be read with sound off — see muted_test.

mandatory.customer_words: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: The hero is an Indian PG owner in his own clothes, not a plumber and not a costume; obstacles are plain concrete cubes with no faces, no eyes and no mushroom or shell forms; there are no coins, no pipes, no blocks with question marks, no brick tiles and no castle; the score is an original chiptune that quotes no existing melody, motif or timbre; the flag is a plain cloth pennant. The negative_line forbids existing game characters and copyrighted assets on every prompt. The genre is borrowed; nothing of the property is.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com. identity_invariants: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground
mandatory.realisation: The supplied wordmark file is placed, never redrawn, recoloured or regenerated — it appears on the phone screen at 9.8 s and on the composed close. The two brand values are load-bearing in the world rather than decorative: #0038FF is the ground he runs on from frame one, and #03FFF1 is the power itself, which is why the product's colour is the one saturated element in a graded-down frame. RENTOK.COM closes the film.

All fifteen supplied strings appear verbatim in copy_deck.strings, each composed by code onto the frame, none generated as pixels and none quoted in any image or video prompt. No string is reflowed, broken across lines, abbreviated or re-cased; the two INSTALL / RENTOK APP pairs are used twice as supplied — once as the cheat code inside the phone, once as the closing ask.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Declared and held on every prompt by the style_line: a chunky matte-plastic 2.5D diorama, one implied ceiling-tube source, high-key flat game light, saturated brand blue ground with everything above it graded down to concrete grey and chalk ochre. One key for the whole film, one light direction, one saturated element.

mandatory.customer_words: Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: The mechanic is kept whole — a collected power-up grants both immunity (he passes through obstacles unharmed) and a ranged effect that clears them, and it is what lets him reach the flag. The instrument is the phone held forward like a torch, throwing a cyan cone; no firearm is depicted, and nothing is killed — obstacles come apart into plates that flatten into the ground he then runs on.

native_audio is on: every beat's sound is generated with its clip (scuffs, latch, cube thuds, cloth snap, room tone) and the original chiptune is laid under it. No dialogue and no voice-over anywhere, per the production constraint — see the declared deviation on the CTA pairing.

All copy is originated in English, the language the supplied strings are given in, and is never a translation of a line written elsewhere; no Devanagari is generated. The India in the frame is named by variables rather than by 'India': the owner of a 30-50 bed PG in an outer-suburb tech belt, 45-60, running the building himself. It is carried by unstyled set detail — steel-framed doors, blue water cans on a rack, a drying line, a tulsi pot in a cut paint tin — not by festival motifs, filmi costume codes or a celebrity.

brand_timeline.in_context: The brand is in the world from frame one without being a logo in frame one: the ground the owner runs on for all 30 seconds is RentOK blue #0038FF, so there is no lapse at any point in the film. The supplied wordmark itself first appears at 9.8 s, on the phone screen in his own hand — inside 10 s, and in use rather than stamped on. It is present again on the phone through beats 5, 6 and 7, and on the composed close from 26.2 to 30.0. Cyan #03FFF1 is established on the product at 13.2-17.4 in the closest shot in the film, which is what lets it read instantly on the moving figure at speed in beat 6. Four asset types carry the brand: the supplied mark, the two brand colours in the set and the power, the product itself on screen and in use, and the composed close.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — this job carries no dialogue and no voice-over, so the name is never said aloud. It is carried by the mark on the phone, by the two brand colours the world is built from, and by the composed ask. Declared as a deviation.

last_frame: The composed close, held still: flat RentOK blue #0038FF, the supplied wordmark unaltered just above centre — Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1 — INSTALL / RENTOK APP beneath it in the lower third, RENTOK.COM one size smaller under that, and the single flat cyan rectangle carried in from the pennant at the right edge. Silent for the last four-tenths of a second.

deviations.from: / / default: set out to be interesting, not funny; no cartoon for adults, no vignette parade; humour only under a brief clause (mla_0064, ogx_0032, whip_0058).
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game... Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity. It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.' The customer specifies a game pastiche, which is a playful register by construction. The clause is used narrowly: the register is play, not jokes — there is no gag, no take to camera, no slapstick, and the humour never carries the selling point, which is carried by the substitution of five checks for five problems.

deviations.from: / / default: the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words, the brand name is spoken as well as shown, and supers equal spoken words (ogx_0042, abcd_0012, abcd_0021).
deviations.brief_clause: The job's production constraints ('no dialogue or voice-over') taken with 'Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts' — feed delivery that autoplays muted. The pairing default is stated on the premise that audio is heard (abcd_0014) and the packs record that the corpus does not say how a sound-off feed carries the ask. Realisation: the on-screen channel carries ask and brand alone, the film is built to pass muted, and the audio layer carries only what it can — emotion and impact.

deviations.from: / / default: the key agrees with one nameable fictional source and follows the dramatic line; a product film is not the exempt genre (alt_0018, alt_0011, ).
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game' and 'Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system' — the brief names a game pastiche, and a game world is lit flat and high-key throughout rather than dropping with the dramatic line. Realisation: the key is declared high and flat for the whole film and never changes with the mood; a fictional source is still named and obeyed for direction (one ceiling tube in the corridor, evening sky on the terrace), and the mood is carried instead by frame width, pace, silence and the grey-to-cyan colour turn.

deviations.from: / default: no running line in all-capitals; all-caps is the hardest read (alb_0005).
deviations.brief_clause: exact_text_strings, every value supplied in capitals with 'may_reflow': false — the customer supplies the strings verbatim and forbids re-setting them. Realisation: kept as supplied, and the cost is paid down where it can be: each is a short label of one to three words rather than a running line, only one is on screen at a time, they are set in a medium-weight humanist sans at large size with generous tracking, and every block is measured at the darkest and lightest point of its actual ground.

deviations.from: / default: consecutive shots of one subject sit at least 30 degrees apart on the arc or change focal length, else they jump (gos_0014); composition differs at every straight cut (gote_0026).
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game.' A side-scroller is read through a single locked profile camera, and that convention is the form the customer asked for. Realisation: beats 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 hold one side-on axis inside a single 180-degree arc and never reverse screen direction; the jump is avoided by changing field size and camera position along the axis rather than by moving around it, and the one genuine grammar break — into the over-shoulder close at 9.8 and back out at 17.4 — is bridged by a change of focal length going in and by the cyan expansion acting as a wipe coming out, which waives the composition and angle requirements at that cut.
